LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Title: Starbound Frontier weapon and shield range
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_NoAccess: Starbound Frontier public-facility access is required.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_TargetUnavailable: The target or its primary shield is unavailable. You may continue the other lessons.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Stage_Range: Optional visit: dock at the west side of the platform’s northwest corner. Follow the gold floor arrow to the instructions terminal and acknowledge the briefing to unlock the blast door. Follow the north-wall terminals west to east for the suggested order. Continue salvage training at any time; no firing is required.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Dialog_Range:
If you can fly that trainer, you have earned the right to complain about it. Before salvage practice, I recommend visiting our weapons and shields range.

This is not an exam. Look around and leave, or continue right now. Starbound Frontier developed kinetic and electromagnetic shields recently for local combat conditions. You may not have seen anything like them before your voyage.

Find the separate weapons platform through the quest targets. Soft-dock at the west side of its northwest corner and bring your captain aboard. Follow the gold floor arrow, select your captain and right-click the instructions terminal. Read and acknowledge the briefing to unlock the blast door. The six terminals along the north wall suggest a west-to-east order: unshielded, kinetic, electromagnetic deflection, reflection, single guard and cooperative guard.

Try that order if you like. You can reopen the guidance and continue salvage training whenever you are ready.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_Unshielded:
Shields are off. The target has multiple layers of plasteel armour, with steel walls behind them to show penetration depth.

Rapid cannon fire accumulates damage through repeated hits. The heavy cannon concentrates more impact into each shell. Lasers hit immediately and spend stored power. The fixed-axis railgun uses three serial accelerators for deep penetration at a high energy cost.

Main groups 1/2/3/4 select those weapons. Try one at a time, compare holes, depth, heat and energy, then change shields. The range does not automatically repair damage or refill ammunition.

The rail axis avoids shield generators. Its test lane has two frontal armour layers, internal bulkheads and a row of empty batteries. Look for a narrow penetration channel through walls and equipment, usually without broad foundation damage. Foundations are not immune.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_Kinetic:
The kinetic line shield is on at full strength. Lasers, missiles and boarding craft pass through it. It does not simply erase incoming rounds.

It applies a paid normal impulse while preserving tangential motion. Only an impulse reaching the projectile fracture threshold breaks it: heavy shells resist, while slender railgun rods fracture easily. Zero strength causes no slowing or fragmentation and charges no pulse cost. Fragments can still damage armour; shattered does not mean harmless.

This is especially efficient against deep-penetrating railgun slugs. Dense rapid fire can drain the battery quickly: each active impulse costs energy, and accelerating light rounds back outward costs additional energy. Underpayment applies only the funded effect and briefly disables the line.

Compare main groups 2, 4 and 1, then use group 3 to see a laser pass through. Select the target battery to inspect its real stored energy.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_Deflection:
The electromagnetic deflection preset is active. It affects lasers only; solid shots, missiles and boarding craft pass through.

At low strength, passive refraction depends on incidence: a straight-on beam does not turn, while oblique beams may bend or even reflect. This preset adds an active turn to send the beam away from the target. Use main group 3 and watch the segmented beam.

Deflection does not delete the beam. It may still hit something else. Larger active turns cost more electricity. The reflection terminal demonstrates a return toward the source. Switching does not refill energy.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_Reflection: Full electromagnetic reflection is selected. If enough energy is available, the beam turns back along its incoming direction. Use main group 3; the platform guard shield catches the returning beam.\n\nReflection is effective, but sustained or high-power lasers demand substantial electricity. Watch the target battery. Underpayment weakens the turn and briefly disables the line. Solid shots, missiles and boarding craft still pass through.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_GuardSingle:
Only the forward guard generator is active; the rear two are off.

Guard shields defend against every attack type except boarding craft. With enough capacity, they stop the incoming attack and keep the hull undamaged. Regular capacity is limited, however. Heavy and railgun fire make that clear; a penetrating round with more impact than the available capacity can continue with its remaining power.

Once regular capacity is exhausted, the generator can spend its local emergency reserve. White means regular and red means emergency. Regular capacity recovers with power after a quiet interval. Emergency capacity does not regenerate and requires substantial silver. Try the cooperative guard terminal to compare several generators.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_Guard:
All three guard generators are now active on the same target ship. Hits on the forward dome distribute regular-capacity costs among the participating generators. Select them to watch their balances fall together.

The rear domes cover only the rear equipment; the forward dome covers the armour. This separates shared capacity from overlapping shield surfaces. Once the shared pool is exhausted, a hit on the forward dome spends only that generator's local emergency reserve. Rear emergency stores cannot pay remotely.

Guard coverage is broad, but capacity is finite and boarding craft pass through. One silver restores five emergency points; filling an empty standard generator takes 150 silver. Kinetic and electromagnetic shields instead spend electricity on the attacks they suit.

No demonstration is required to progress. Reopen the survival briefing and continue salvage whenever you want.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_EntranceUnavailable: The entrance blast door is unavailable. You can still continue the other lessons.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_Introduction:
Welcome to the Starbound Frontier weapons range. Read this before entering through the blast door.

FIRING CONTROLS
Select the platform console or another building on it, verify that the sidebar has selected the test platform, expand combat controls and choose manual fire control. Main and secondary sets each have six switches; highlighted groups are enabled. Left-click fires the main set, right-click the secondary set. Keep the pointer over the map rather than the interface.

Automatic fire control selects hostile targets; this allied target requires manual fire control. Disabled fire control stops all weapons, independently of piloting. 

Main groups 1, 2, 3 and 4 are rapid fire, heavy cannon, laser and railgun. Enable one at a time for comparisons. Switching active groups does not alter weapon configuration. Turrets have advanced auto-aim and need no gunner; the railgun fires along its fixed axis. Cooldown, overheating, ammunition or stored-energy shortages can prevent firing. Select the equipment to inspect its state.

KEEP THE STATION OUT OF IT
This is an allied public facility. You may operate fire control and switch active weapon groups, but cannot change firing arcs, range, power, charge or other weapon settings. For safety, firing arcs are restricted to the target ship to the east. Dismantling station equipment will also cost goodwill.

SUGGESTED ORDER
Past the blast door, follow the north-wall terminals west to east: unshielded, kinetic, electromagnetic deflection, reflection, single guard, cooperative guard. Compare armour first, then shields. Presets do not repair the target or refill ammunition, energy or shield capacity. Batteries and regular shields recover normally; emergency capacity requires silver.

The rail axis crosses two frontal armour layers, internal bulkheads and a row of empty test batteries, avoiding the shield generators. Observe a narrow penetration path through walls and equipment, usually without stripping a broad area of hull foundations. Foundations are not immune. Test batteries are isolated from the working grid so electrical explosions do not obscure the effect. Stay off the target ship.

A TESTER’S WISH
Our testers often say: “If only this worked like a game with save files. We could save before testing, then reload if we wrecked the target and wanted to try something else.”

They insist it is a joke. I am certainly not hinting at anything.

Acknowledge this briefing to unlock the entrance. Neither visiting nor firing is an exam; you may continue salvage training at any time.
